title: Walsh character is unchanged by appending an unused coordinate
statement:
Fix $n\in\bbn$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $b\in\{0,1\}$. Form the
point $(x,b)\in\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending $b$ as the final coordinate, and
regard $S$ as a subset $S'\subseteq[n+1]$ via the inclusion $[n]\hookrightarrow[n+1]$
that leaves each index fixed (so the new last coordinate never lies in $S'$). Then the
Walsh--Fourier character of $S'$ evaluated at the extended point agrees with that of $S$
at the original point:
\[
  \chi_{S'}\big((x,b)\big) \;=\; \chi_S(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: subset S of the index set [n]
point x in the Boolean cube {0,1}^n
bit b appended as the final coordinate
S lifted to [n+1] by the coordinate-fixing inclusion
replaced:
For a subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, a point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, and a bit $b$,
the parity character of the lifted set equals the character of $S$ on $x$:
\[
  \chi_{\,\mathrm{castSucc}(S)}(\mathrm{snoc}\,x\,b) = \chi_S(x).
\]
That is, appending a last coordinate $b$ and not including it in the set leaves the
character unchanged.
